newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan oil exec says not for exploration of isles.
newsitem.headline: Japan oil exec says not for exploration of isles.

text.p: A senior official of the semi-governmental Japan National Oil Corp (JNOC) said on Friday that he is not urging joint oil exploration of disputed islands in the East China Sea.

Akira Sakurai, vice president and a member of the JNOC board, also denied having said that joint exploration of the islands -- known as the Diaoyus to the Chinese and Senkakus to the Japanese -- could help ease tensions in the area.
Reuters reported from Singapore on Wednesday that Sakurai had said joint exploration could help ease tensions over the islands.
He said on Friday that he had made a reference to regions in Asia where field activity had been frozen despite their potential as oil reserves because of territorial disputes.
But he said, however, that he had not intended his comments to be taken as a call for the early development of such areas.
"I was speaking on the premise that such exploration activities could not take place until the government resolved such issues," Sakurai said.
"I was saying that private oil companies, who were the (main) participants of the conference, needed to urge their governments (to work on resolving the issue)," he said.
JNOC is affiliated with the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI).
